question: Should OpenClaw reserve the top-level `auth` CLI root for core, even when an installed plugin already owns that root?
rationale: The patch cannot preserve both current plugin-root ownership and an unconditional built-in `auth` command without an explicit namespace policy or new collision-resolution design.

options.title: Preserve plugin ownership
options.body: Keep `models auth list` canonical or redesign the alias so an installed plugin-owned `auth` root continues to win.

options.title: Reserve auth for core
options.body: Explicitly make `auth` a core-reserved namespace and require compatibility documentation plus upgrade and collision proof.

options.title: Close the shortcut
options.body: Decline the extra alias because the existing canonical command already provides the capability without expanding the core namespace.

recommendation.title: Preserve plugin ownership
recommendation.body: Keep `models auth list` canonical or redesign the alias so an installed plugin-owned `auth` root continues to win.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing signal in the current PR and adjacent plugin-CLI context, though direct historical ownership remains uncertain.
